info.name: TracePilot API
info.description:
Smoke and hardening tests for TracePilot.

1. Start TracePilot (`go -C backend run ./cmd/tracepilot serve`) and set the variables below if your ports differ.
2. Run folders 1-6 in order with the Collection Runner (or send requests one by one).
3. Folder 2 registers `accountEmail` (or signs in), makes a project for the run and an ingest token for it. Telemetry is sent with that ingest token; everything is read back as the account that owns the project.

There are no API keys: people sign in with a JWT access token, applications send telemetry with an ingest token. Production endpoints use HTTPS: change baseUrl and otlpUrl.

request.description: In production this needs a signed-in person with a role in the project; in development it is open.

item.name: 2. Account, project and ingest token
item.description:
Registers (or signs in) and makes a project for this run. Everything after this folder works in that project, so a run never touches other people's data.

The development-only `tracepilot seed` creates only a super administrator; it does not create projects, environments, memberships, or demo telemetry. Server startup does not create a default project. On an installation, set accountEmail/accountPassword to yours or use the seeded admin, or leave them: a new account is registered when registration is open.

exec: pm.test('says whether registration is open', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().registration_open).to.be.a('boolean'); });
pm.test('created, already registered, or registration closed', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([201, 409, 403]); });

request.description: Saves accessToken (15 minutes). The refresh token is an HttpOnly cookie that only the /api/v1/auth routes receive.

exec: pm.test('access token is a JWT and the password hash is never returned', function () { pm.expect(b.access_token.split('.')).to.have.length(3); pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('pbkdf2'); });
pm.test('the refresh token is not in the body', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('refresh'); });

item.name: Create the project for this run

request.description: Any registered account may create a project; a regular account may own up to ten.
Saves ingestToken for the OTLP requests. The secret is shown only once.

exec: pm.test('secret returned once, as a JWT', function () { pm.expect(b.jwt.split('.')).to.have.length(3); });
pm.test('the list never contains the secret', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('ingestToken')); });

request.description: ClickHouse is required for log storage: raw logs persist to ClickHouse time-based UTC partitions (daily, monthly, yearly, or weekly). ACK waits for ClickHouse flush and the PostgreSQL incident/outbox transaction; transient failures return 503 for exporter retry. The existing verify folder reads logs through the same API. For an existing database, stop ingestion, migrate clickhouse up, then migrate clickhouse backfill before restarting.

item.description: Sends telemetry with the ingest token. It lands in this run's project, in its first environment (add `X-Environment: <name>` to choose another). Event batches wait for durable storage and make at most three storage attempts, with backoff only between attempts; cancelling the worker during backoff stops further writes. Transient storage failures still return 503/Unavailable for exporter retry.

item.name: 4. Verify what was stored (signed in as the owner)

request.description: Fails if any of the credentials sent by 'Logs: free-text secrets' is stored. Needs ScrubFreeText enabled (the default).

item.name: Live stream: SSE connection
item.description: Manual SSE check. Set runLiveStream=true to enable; it is skipped in normal collection runs. Sends the access JWT, project and staging environment. The connection expires with its JWT, rechecks account/membership every 15s (2s check timeout), and bounds each frame write to 5s. Revoked access or a failed check closes it. At most 256 streams per process; live delivery is best effort and local to that process.

item.name: OTLP with a console access token -> 401

request.description: A token for the console is not accepted as a telemetry credential.

item.name: Management API with an ingest token -> 401

request.description: An ingest token cannot read anything.

item.name: A project you do not belong to -> 403

request.description: An unknown project answers exactly like one you cannot open.

item.name: OTLP body over the size limit -> 413

request.description: 5 MiB, above the default 4 MiB ingestion.max_request_bytes.

Run only this request, 65 iterations, no delay. After 60 failures from one address OTLP answers 429 without touching the database. WARNING: the whole address is blocked for the next minute, valid keys included. Wait one minute before the other folders.

6. Roles, members and sessions
item.description:
Two people in one project: the owner made it, the user was let in. Then the refresh token rotation and sign-out.

Send the refresh requests with the cookie jar enabled (Postman app; newman keeps it for a run). The cookie belongs to the account that signed in or registered last.

exec: pm.test('same answer as an unknown account', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql('INVALID_CREDENTIALS'); });

request.description: Without X-TracePilot-Refresh a cross-site form could have sent the cookie, so it is refused.

exec: pm.test('a cookie alone is not enough', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql('UNAUTHORIZED'); });

request.description: Each refresh also replaces the refresh cookie; the old one stops working.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('memberToken', b.access_token); pm.collectionVariables.set('memberUserId', b.user.id); }

request.description: Registering does not give access to anyone's project.

item.name: A user cannot create ingest tokens -> 403

exec: pm.test('one owner and one user', function () { const roles = pm.response.json().data.map(function (m) { return m.role; }).sort(); pm.expect(roles).to.eql(['owner', 'user']); });

pm.test('records who changed access', function () { const actions = pm.response.json().data.map(function (e) { return e.action; }); pm.expect(actions).to.include.members(['member.added', 'project.created', 'ingest_token.created']); });
